A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NcPU research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on five datasets, component ablations, hyperparameter analyses, and representation visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds training-stability curves, imbalance experiments, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same NoiSNCL loss, PLD, PhantomGate, and updating procedures. The new similarity-clipping suggestion is numerical-stability advice, not an established implementation change; masked image modeling is future work.

E1.justification: The five datasets and binary classification tasks remain unchanged. Appendix H adds low-positive-prevalence CIFAR-10 scenarios with class priors of 0.05 and 0.1, extending coverage to substantially different class mixtures within an existing dataset.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing experiments retain their comparator sets. The new imbalance and cost analyses reuse WSC, nnPU, and LaGAM, which were already evaluated in v1. The newly cited CoTAP loss is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: New protocols reduce labeled-positive counts to obtain imbalance ratios of 80 and 53.33, and use 20,000 unlabeled samples for the low-prior tests. Table 12 introduces training-time, inference-latency, and GFLOPs measurements. The original 1300-epoch training budget remains unchanged.

E4.justification: The supplementary analyses expand substantially beyond the retained component and hyperparameter studies. v2 investigates prolonged-training stability on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, robustness to positive-label scarcity and low positive prevalence, and computational tradeoffs against existing methods (Figure 6 and Tables 10–12).

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated three times and report means and standard deviations. The new accuracy tables follow that practice; no changed run counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results remain unchanged, while focused supplementary results are added. At imbalance ratio 80, NcPU/WSC OA is 93.70/81.46; at class prior 0.05 it is 93.57/90.97. Table 12 adds training times of 14.84 seconds per epoch for NcPU versus 14.79 for LaGAM, 16.00 for WSC, and 5.06 for nnPU. These are new findings, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its vMF and uniform-prior assumptions, and the Appendix B derivations are retained. The added stability discussion applies the existing gradient expression near unit similarity rather than supplying a new theorem, proof, or revised derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central representation-learning bottleneck, NoiSNCL–PLD contribution, EM interpretation, and empirical superiority claims. The new masked-image-modeling sentence describes future work rather than an achieved contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting architectural asymmetry and gradient behavior to training stability, interprets the imbalance results as robustness evidence, and explains comparable inference costs through use of a single classifier. The earlier caveat about occasional training instability remains.

D1.justification: The abstract and reproducibility statement replace the promised future code release with a concrete repository address. v2 also supplies computational-cost information and an optional similarity-clipping interval. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters in Appendices E–F remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Wen et al. (2025) and discusses CoTAP's semantic alignment and weighting of high-scoring pairs. The broader positioning against contrastive PU methods and WSC remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to added discussion, a computational-overhead appendix, minor wording, and publication, author-contact, and corresponding-author information. Most prose and section organization are retained. Appendix G introduces an unresolved 'Table ??' reference.

P2.justification: v2 adds the training-stability plot as Figure 6 and three tables for imbalance and computational cost. Existing figures retain their content but later figures are renumbered; surrounding text and appendix material reflow within the same document template.

improvement.justification: The added stability and imbalance evidence modestly strengthens empirical support, while cost reporting and a concrete code-access pointer improve practical usefulness. The original method, proofs, and results are preserved. These gains are limited by the narrow added benchmark coverage and unspecified timing hardware, with a small presentation regression from Appendix G's broken table reference.
